issues.title: GeometryCollection.geoms loses element type information under Pyright strict mode
issues.body:
When narrowing a BaseGeometry using isinstance(geometry, GeometryCollection), Pyright cannot infer the type of elements returned by geometry.geoms.
The elements are inferred as Any, triggering strict typing diagnostics.
By contrast, an explicitly parameterized GeometryCollection[BaseGeometry] correctly returns BaseGeometry elements . The Multi* version returns the corresponding elements (MultiLineString.geoms -> LineString and so on).
Expected behavior
Iterating over GeometryCollection.geoms should provide at least BaseGeometry as the element type, without requiring explicit generic parameters or casts.
Actual behavior
Pyright reports reportUnknownMemberType and reportUnknownVariableType after narrowing with isinstance.
Workaround
Instead of calling directly isinstance method, this function can be called and the types are not complaining anymore.
def is_geometry_collection(
    geometry: BaseGeometry,
) -> TypeGuard[GeometryCollection[BaseGeometry]]:
    return isinstance(geometry, GeometryCollection)

Reproduction
The base repro.py
"""Minimal static typing reproduction for Shapely GeometryCollection.geoms.

Run `uv run pyright` (do not execute this file with Python).
"""
from typing import reveal_type

from shapely.geometry import GeometryCollection, MultiLineString
from shapely.geometry.base import BaseGeometry


def reproduced_issue(geometry: BaseGeometry) -> None:
    if isinstance(geometry, GeometryCollection):
        reveal_type(geometry.geoms)
        for part in geom

issues.body:
We regularly run into Floating-point Exceptions being set by code in GEOS. The NumPy ufunc machinery then picks this up and turns it into a python RuntimeWarning visible for the user (but one they cannot do anything about it, since it happens inside the GEOS code). While the warning is typically harmless, it is still confusing for the user to see and annoying to have to silence.
Some examples: pygeos/pygeos#404, pygeos/pygeos#167, #1345, #1552, #1709, #1840, #2045, #2215
Several of those have been reported upstream to GEOS and sometimes also fixed (libgeos/geos#515, libgeos/geos#806, libgeos/geos#1048, libgeos/geos#1235, libgeos/geos#1492, libgeos/geos#1555)
But addressing this upstream in GEOS is often not that easy to diagnose and fix (and it also does not always result in a real improvement to the GEOS code, since sometimes the exceptions get set due to compiler optimizations or are hardware/compiler dependent).
We could also suppress those on the Shapely side (essentially call feclearexcept at the end of each ufunc inner function after any GEOS interaction (or catch/restore the flag), such that NumPy does not see the flag)
That would, with a relatively simple change, do away with all those warning related issues. At the same time it would suppress potentially actionable warnings (where there is an actual issue in the GEOS code). I am opening this issue to try to summarize the current state of the transform API in shapely, triggered by reviewing its docs for the upcoming shapely 2.2 release. Apologies for the long issue, I tried to keep it as short as possible while still being clear and complete ;)
Related previous discussions: #1668, #1676, #1902 (and open issue about better documenting both: #1897)
Context
When applying a generic function on the coordinates (i.e. not using one of the shapely.affinity transformations), there are various ways how this function can work and be called. Copying from my comment at #1668 (comment), possible "degrees of freedom" on how to apply the function are:

How to pass the coordinates to the function:
a. Pass them as a single argument (a single tuple, or a 2D array in case of multiple coordinates)
b. Pass them as separate x, y(, z) arguments (single scalars, or separate 1D arrays/lists in case of multiple coordinates)

a. Apply the function on all coordinates of all geometries at once
b. Apply the function once per geometry
c. Apply the function once per coordinate sequence
d. Apply the function once per coordinate pair

Historically, the shapely.ops.transform(func, geom) function has always used passed coordinates as separate arguments (1b) and first tried to pass coordinates as a tuple per coord sequence and if that errors, per coord pair (2c with fallback to 2d).

issues.title: `buffer()` with an almost-zero distance removes polygon holes
issues.body:
Calling Polygon.buffer() with an extremely small non-zero distance removes a valid interior ring. The distance (1e-17) is many orders of magnitude too small to close the hole geometrically.
Reproducible example
import shapely
from shapely.geometry import Polygon

polygon = Polygon(
    shell=[(0, 0), (10, 0), (10, 10), (0, 10)],
    holes=[[(2, 2), (8, 2), (8, 8), (2, 8)]],
)

buffered = polygon.buffer(1e-17, cap_style='flat', join_style='mitre')

print(polygon.wkt)
print(buffered.wkt)
Actual behavior
The original WKT contains the interior ring, but the WKT produced by buffered does not: the hole is removed.
POLYGON ((0 0, 10 0, 10 10, 0 10, 0 0), (2 2, 8 2, 8 8, 2 8, 2 2))
POLYGON ((-1e-17 -1e-17, -1e-17 10, 10 10, 10 -1e-17, -1e-17 -1e-17))

Expected behavior
A buffer distance of 1e-17 should preserve this hole. A positive buffer may shrink holes, but this distance is far too small relative to the geometry dimensions to eliminate a 6-by-6 hole.
Environment

Operating system: Windows-10-10.0.26200-SP0
Python: 3.11.1
Shapely: 2.1.1
GEOS: 3.13.1

issues.title: Documentation: clarify that hausdorff_distance measures vertex-to-polyline distance not polyline-to-polyline distance

The documentation for hausdorff_distance states that it computes:

"the furthest distance that a point on either geometry can be from the nearest point to it on the other geometry."

That is, if measuring the distance from polyline A to polyline B and the vertices of these polylines are denoted $v_A$ and $v_B$, the documentation suggests that the value computed is:

$$H_{A \to B}$$

$$H_{v_A \to B}$$

issues.title: Allow a Mapping to add headers to the request sent to an HTTP AuthService
issues.body:
Please describe your use case / problem.
An AuthService applies to every Mapping in the cluster, so it's often useful to provide per-Mapping context to the service.
Emissary already supports this for gRPC auth services through Mapping.auth_context_extensions, which becomes check_settings.context_extensions on the route.
This is limited to gRPC as Envoy only sends context_extensions in a gRPC CheckRequest.
For HTTP auth services there is no per-Mapping option:

Mapping.add_request_headers becomes the route's request_headers_to_add, which Envoy's router applies after the ext_authz filter has run, so the auth service never sees those headers.
AuthService.add_auth_headers becomes authorization_request.headers_to_add on the listener-level filter, so it applies to every route.
Mapping.auth_context_extensions is written into the config, but Envoy ignores it for an http_service.

Describe the solution you'd like
Add add_auth_headers to Mapping resources, with the same meaning as on an AuthService. These are added to the request Emissary sends to the auth service when checking requests that match the Mapping.
apiVersion: getambassador.io/v3alpha1
kind: Mapping
metadata:
  name: quote-backend
spec:
  prefix: /backend/
  service: quote
  add_auth_headers:
    x-tenant: team-a

issues.title: v4 releases keep /v3 module path
issues.body:
Summary
The v4.x.x releases are tagged on a module whose path still ends in /v3:
// go.mod
module github.com/emissary-ingress/emissary/v3

Per Go's module version numbering rules, any module at major version ≥ 2 must have a matching /vN suffix in its module path. A v4.x.x tag on a /v3 module path is invalid, so Go tooling cannot resolve these releases.
Reproduction
$ go get github.com/emissary-ingress/emissary/v3@v4.1.0
go: github.com/emissary-ingress/emissary/v3@v4.1.0: invalid version: module contains a go.mod file, so module path must match major version ("github.com/emissary-ingress/emissary/v4")
There is no path that resolves the v4 tags:

.../emissary/v3@v4.1.0 → rejected (major mismatch, as above)
.../emissary/v4@v4.1.0 → 404, no such module path published

Result: consumers are stuck on v3.x.x and cannot import any code from a v4 release.
Impact
Emissary is imported as a library by downstream projects — e.g. external-dns depends on pkg/api/getambassador for the Mapping/Host CRD types (kubernetes-sigs/external-dns#6482). These consumers cannot upgrade to v4.

issues.title: AWS Managed Prometheus (AMP) rejects instant queries with >31d lookback range
issues.body:
When using --eks-managed-prom with --history_duration greater than ~720h (30 days), KRR fails with:
HTTP Status Code 422: "queries with long day range (32d to 95d) are currently
only supported for range type queries"
Root cause:
In prometheus_metrics_service.py, pod owner lookup queries are capped at 32 days:
days_literal = min(int(period.total_seconds()) // 3600 // 24, 32)
period_literal = f"{days_literal}d"
This generates an instant query like kube_replicaset_owner{...}[32d]. AMP does not support instant queries with a lookback ≥ 32 days. However, AMP does support query_range for periods up to 95 days.
Expected behavior:
KRR should use query_range endpoint (range query) for long history lookups instead of instant queries, similar to how CPULoader explicitly sets query_type: QueryType.QueryRange.
Suggested fix:
Use QueryType.QueryRange for the pod owner lookup, or split the query into smaller chunks.
Environment:
KRR v1.28.0
AWS Managed Prometheus (AMP)
--history_duration 960 (40 days)

issues.title: Feature request: allow non-admin users to manage their own API keys
issues.body:
Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.
Today API keys can only be handled through "Manage API keys", and that permission covers every key:

on create the user field is free, and on edit it can be changed, so anyone with the permission can make a key that acts as any other user, superusers included;
the API Keys list returns the key value of every key.

Because of that we can only give it to admins. When a technician needs API access (scripts, automation), an admin has to create the key and then hand it over, and the admin keeps seeing everyone's keys.
Describe the solution you'd like
A new role permission, e.g. "Manage own API keys". For a non-superuser who has it:

the list shows only their own keys;
create always assigns the key to the requesting user (the user field is ignored);
edit and delete work only on their own keys, and the user can't be changed.

"Manage API keys" would keep working as it does today for admins.
Describe alternatives you've considered
Admins create the key and hand it over through a password manager. It works, but it doesn't scale and the admin sees every key.
Additional context
We run 1.5.2 with SSO-only login and a role per technician. If this sounds acceptable, I can open a PR against develop (API + tacticalrmm-web + tests).

issues.title: Minimum compatibility and official support for SNI Passthrough reverse proxy deployments
issues.body:
Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.
Yes. Tactical RMM currently does not appear to officially support reverse proxy deployments.
This creates a limitation for small and medium-sized businesses, MSPs, and on-premises infrastructures that do not have a dedicated public IP address available exclusively for Tactical RMM.
In my infrastructure, several public services share the same internet entry point. I already have a front-facing proxy/gateway server responsible for receiving inbound HTTPS traffic and routing it to the correct internal service. Because Tactical RMM uses multiple services and subdomains, such as the web panel, API, and MeshCentral, terminating TLS at the external proxy and forwarding HTTP internally is not ideal.
For this reason, I adopted an SNI Passthrough approach. The external proxy does not decrypt HTTPS traffic. It only inspects the TLS SNI hostname and forwards the TCP connection to the Tactical RMM server, allowing Tactical RMM to keep control of TLS termination, certificates, WebSocket behavior, and its internal expected configuration.
This solution is currently working well in my environment, but because it is not officially documented or supported, there is a risk that a future Tactical RMM release may change behavior and unintentionally break this deployment model.
Describe the solution you'd like
I would like Tactical RMM to officially recognize and minimally support SNI Passthrough reverse proxy deployments as a valid dep
